results.fact: Whether a self-issue wilderness permit is required at this trailhead
results.correct_value: No wilderness permit is required to hike or camp in the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness; a Northwest Forest Pass / interagency pass is needed to park at the trailhead. NPS backcountry permits apply only to overnight stays inside the North Cascades NP Complex.
results.evidence: The Okanogan-Wenatchee NF wilderness page states for Lake Chelan-Sawtooth: 'Wilderness permit not required to hike or camp including on the Lakeshore Trail.' The Recreation.gov point-of-interest page for the wilderness states 'No wilderness permits are need to camp or hike in this area', noting only trailhead parking passes. The FS Lake Chelan-Sawtooth page limits permit requirements to overnight stays in the North Cascades NP Complex (a backcountry permit, not a self-issue one) and Lake Chelan dock sites. The row's own Scatter Lake bivy entry already says no permit is needed.

results.fact: Approach mileage/gain figures citing the wrong route's trailhead (Scatter Lake)
results.evidence: The Scatter Lake figures are genuine for the standard south-side route (9.2 mi RT and 3,850 ft to the 7,047 ft lake, so ~11 mi / ~5,200 ft to the summit), and Wolf Creek/Gardner Meadows is the documented way onto the north ridge (a Wolf Creek TH trip went via Gardner Meadows, the abandoned mine trail, the dried tarn with cabin remnants, a spur ridge and the mine on the crest; 34 mi / 8,000 ft for a three-peak outing). But which approach this route row should present is itself unsettled (see the discovered approach contradiction), so the partner_requirements figures cannot be replaced until that is decided; no source found describing a North Creek approach to the north ridge.

results.fact: Round-trip distance: dist_km vs itinerary miles
results.evidence: dist_km is the one-way approach (6.9 km = 4.3 mi) and itinerary miles are the day's round trip (8.7 mi); 2 x 4.3 = 8.6, consistent within rounding.

results.fact: Which approach/trailhead the North Ridge uses: approach/itinerary/timing say North Creek Trail #413 from the Gilbert (North Creek) trailhead at ~3,660 ft with a mine trail at mile 2; approach_variants/detailed_rack/what_to_bring say every recorded ascent comes via Wolf Creek and Gardner Meadows and the North Creek side is undescribed; the Trailhead waypoint is named Scatter Creek Trailhead at 3,150 ft (coordinates at Scatter Creek) yet its note calls it the start of North Creek Trail #413; bivy says the north ridge is reached from the Scatter Lake basin
results.evidence: Documented north-ridge ascents found start at the Wolf Creek trailhead and go via Gardner Meadows, the old USFS mine trail, a dried tarn with cabin remnants, a spur ridge and mine debris on the crest. No source found for a mine trail leaving North Creek Trail #413 at ~mile 2 to a saddle 0.6 mi north of the summit; North Creek Trail #413 runs to North Lake and Abernathy Pass, and the only mine trail found off it lies above North Lake, far from Abernathy's north saddle. The approach, itinerary, timing, trailhead waypoint and gain/distance all hang on this choice, so nothing was patched.

results.correct_value: Three rappels is one party's documented count; another party needed two. 'Two or three' in climbing_route accurately reflects that range and does not conflict with the three-rappel description.
results.evidence: One detailed ascent report left the summit and 'made three rappels to reach the upper gully'. A separate 2020 ascent report describes two rappels off the Agnes summit block. The count depends on rope length and anchor choice, so both figures are real.

results.fact: overall grade (Class 3-4) vs the route's own technical crux (5.6-5.8, roped, rappelled)
results.evidence: External sources agree that the line this row's body describes (Asa Peak NE ridge to Agnes's south ridge) has roped climbing: technical sections up to 5.6 on the recommended route; a 5.8 chimney crux in one ascent report; a 5.6 chimney crux in another. So 'Class 3-4' is wrong for that line. But the row's name, overview, fa, beta and face claim the separate 1936 West Fork Agnes Creek line, whose grade was not found. The correct grade depends on the unresolved route-identity decision, and changing it would also mean changing grade_system/grade_num and the Class 3-4 wording in partner_requirements/seasonal_hazards. So no patch was made.

results.fact: route identity: claimed 1936 'West Fork of Agnes Creek' line vs the actual body content describing the Asa Peak NE Ridge/South Ridge line
results.evidence: Sources confirm both halves as separate facts. The 1936 first ascent by W. Ronald Frazier and Dan O'Brien went up from the West Fork of Agnes Creek. The recommended/standard route is different: Asa Peak's NE ridge, then a traverse to Agnes's south ridge. Modern ascent reports use Agnes Creek/Spruce Creek, Upper Blue Basin and Icy-Spruce Pass, not the West Fork. This row's body (approach, climbing_route, approach_variants, descent_text, rappel_detail) duplicates wa_agnes_mountain_south_ridge, while its name/overview/fa/beta/face claim the West Fork FA line. Whether this row should become the West Fork line or be merged into the South Ridge row is a catalog decision research cannot make.

results.fact: total gain: 4,000 ft (column) vs 6,700 ft (itinerary sum) / ~6,500 ft (totalNote)
results.evidence: One ascent report gives 34 miles and 13,000 ft gained and lost, i.e. ~6,500 ft of gain. Another gives ~6,598 ft of gain (1,600 ft at High Bridge to the summit) over 33.2 mi RT. Even the arithmetic floor from High Bridge (~1,600 ft) to the ~8,119 ft summit exceeds 6,500 ft, so 4,000 is impossible. 6,500 matches the row's loss_ft and totalNote.

results.fact: access.parking_pass names an unrelated trailhead system (Mountain Loop Highway)
results.correct_value: No trailhead parking (no road access to High Bridge); the only parking is at Fields Point Landing, where the boat is boarded, at $9/night or $45/week overnight.
results.evidence: The NPS fees page for North Cascades says there is no entrance fee; parking or transportation fees may apply. The FS Fields Point Landing page lists overnight parking at $9 per vehicle per day or $45 per 5-7 days. The Stehekin ferry's Fields Point page gives the same $9/night or $45/week. Stehekin/High Bridge has no road connection, so the Mountain Loop Highway pass text is foreign to this route.

results.fact: bivy list mostly for unrelated peaks
results.evidence: Zone list copied across the Stehekin corridor. Serve this route's actual approach: High Bridge Camp (start), Swamp Creek Camp (the day-1 camp used on the Agnes Creek/Spruce Creek approach), Purple Point/Harlequin (boat/shuttle logistics only). Serve the West Fork FA line rather than the body's approach: Fivemile Camp and the West Fork Agnes Creek bivy. Do not serve Agnes: Company Creek/Hilgard Pass (Flora Mountain). results.fact: Summit elevation: waypoint elev/elevFt and itinerary totalNote say 8,131 ft; schedule says 8,131-8,198; high_point_ft says 8,119; bivy says 8,115
results.evidence: Sources disagree. The encyclopedia entry gives 8,119 ft (NAVD88), a peak-list database gives 8,133 ft, one ascent report gives 8,115 ft, and another gives 8,198 ft. There are not two independent agreeing figures, so no patch.

results.fact: Overnight permit on the Agnes Creek corridor: access.permit/access.fees say only the first ~2 mi need an NPS permit and the high camps take a free self-issue USFS permit; itinerary.cal and the Fivemile/Swamp Creek bivy permit texts say a North Cascades NP backcountry permit is required for camps along the Agnes Creek/PCT corridor; access.fees calls the NPS permit free while the NPS lists $10/person + $6
results.evidence: Agnes Gorge trail sources put the NPS/Glacier Peak Wilderness boundary within about a mile of High Bridge. The O-W NF wilderness page says Glacier Peak Wilderness visitors are only asked to sign the trailhead register, while another FS trailhead page describes a free self-issue permit. A camping directory lists Five Mile Camp as a North Cascades NP camp. The NPS fees page lists $10/person plus a $6 fee for backcountry permits. Sources conflict on the camps' jurisdiction and on register vs permit, so nothing was patched.
